text: Why does the opposite-end two-pointer pair-sum search need the array to be sorted?
options: Sorting tells you which pointer to move: a small sum needs a bigger left value, a large sum needs a smaller right value
Sorting removes duplicate values, which would break the pointers
Only sorted arrays can be indexed from both ends
Sorting lets the pointers jump by binary search instead of one step
answer: Sorting tells you which pointer to move: a small sum needs a bigger left value, a large sum needs a smaller right value

text: How much extra space does reversing an array in place with two pointers (swap `a[l]` and `a[r]`, then move both inward) use?

Same-direction pointers: a write index for the next non-zero slot and a read index scanning the array
Binary search for the first zero, then shift everything after it
answer: Same-direction pointers: a write index for the next non-zero slot and a read index scanning the array

text: In Floyd's cycle detection, a slow pointer moves one step and a fast pointer moves two steps. What shows the list has a cycle?

text: In "container with most water", the two-pointer solution always moves the pointer at the shorter line. Why is that safe?
options: Keeping the shorter line can't give a larger area: the width shrinks while the height stays capped by that shorter line
The shorter line has already been paired with every other line
Moving the shorter line keeps the width the same
The next area is always larger after moving the shorter line
answer: Keeping the shorter line can't give a larger area: the width shrinks while the height stays capped by that shorter line

The largest values must be placed first so the loop ends early
Writing from the back never overwrites a value of `nums1` that hasn't been read yet
Writing from the front would need `nums2` to be reversed first
answer: Writing from the back never overwrites a value of `nums1` that hasn't been read yet

text: Floyd's algorithm finds where slow and fast meet inside a cycle. How do you then find the node where the cycle starts?
options: The meeting node is always the cycle start
Move the fast pointer three steps at a time until it reaches the head
Count the cycle length and step that many nodes from the meeting node
Put one pointer back at the head, then move both one step at a time; they meet at the cycle start
answer: Put one pointer back at the head, then move both one step at a time; they meet at the cycle start
